summary: Travellers who are not visa-exempt can buy a US$30 tourist visa on arrival, good for 30 days and extendable once, while citizens of the EU (except Ireland) and the other Schengen states enter visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180 under the EU agreement and citizens of Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand visa-free for 30 days. The Migration Service says the visa on arrival can be obtained at all official border posts open to foreign nationals and staffed by the Migration Service, land crossings included.

Migration Service of Timor-Leste — At the Border (entry conditions)

fee.text: The fee is US$30, paid in US$ cash

entries.text: It is valid for a single entry, thirty days stay and may be extended once for the same period.

extendable.text: In normal circumstances, the Tourist Visa may be extended once only, for a further stay period of 30 days.

visaTypes.name: Tourist Visa applied for before arrival

fee.notes: Apply at a Timorese embassy or consulate abroad. Required only for travellers previously refused entry, removed or excluded, or with unpaid fines; everyone else may obtain the tourist visa on arrival.

source.name: Migration Service of Timor-Leste — Tourist Visa

fee.text: The fee is US$30, paid in US$ cash

entries.text: It is valid for a single entry, thirty days stay and may be extended once for the same period.

fee.notes: Apply in person at the Migration Service Headquarters in Dili. In normal circumstances a tourist visa may be extended once only, for a further stay period of 30 days. Where the application is lodged more than 15 days before the current visa expires, the counting of that visa's validity is suspended.

source.name: Migration Service of Timor-Leste — Tourist Visa

stayDays.text: In normal circumstances, the Tourist Visa may be extended once only, for a further stay period of 30 days.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Timor-Leste.

source.name: Migration Service of Timor-Leste — At the Border (entry conditions, traveller declaration)

alsoStatedOn.name: Migration Service of Timor-Leste — Tourist Visa (documentary requirements: "valid for at least 6 months at the date of entry")

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel insurance requirement for entry to Timor-Leste; the Migration Service's entry conditions and visa documents do not include it. The UK Foreign Office says medical services are limited and a medical emergency is likely to mean evacuation to Australia or Singapore.

source.name: Migration Service of Timor-Leste — Tourist Visa

alsoStatedOn.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Timor-Leste travel advice: health

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read states that every visitor must hold an onward ticket. The Migration Service says visa-on-arrival applicants must present evidence of departure arrangements, such as an onwards transportation ticket or booking, if requested, and lists it among the documents for a tourist visa applied for at an embassy or consulate.

source.name: Migration Service of Timor-Leste — Tourist Visa

proofOfFunds.text: Every visitor must have access to funds sufficient for the stay and may be asked to show them. For tourist, transit and business (Class 1) visa holders not sponsored by family or another contact in the country, the law sets US$100 per entry plus US$50 per day of stay.

source.name: Migration Service of Timor-Leste — At the Border (entry conditions, traveller declaration)

declarations.name: Arrival and departure declaration (Customs Trade Single Window)
declarations.text: All travellers must complete an official declaration online before arrival and before departure. One form serves Migration, Customs, quarantine, the Ministry of Health and the Central Bank. Keep the QR code or PDF to show border officials.

source.name: Migration Service of Timor-Leste — At the Border (entry conditions, traveller declaration)

currencyLimits.text: The customs e-Passenger Declaration that every traveller submits asks whether you carry more than US$5,000 or the equivalent in other currencies; if you do, you must declare the exact amount to Customs. If you carry more than US$20,000 or the equivalent, you must also show Customs the Central Bank of Timor-Leste's authorisation to import that amount.

source.name: Timor-Leste Customs Authority — e-Passenger Declaration (arrival), Goods Questions step

conflict.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Timor-Leste travel advice: entry requirements
conflict.states: Central Bank authorisation for cash or travellers cheques worth USD 20,000 or more, obtained before you arrive

notes: The UK Foreign Office says there are strict rules about goods you can take into or out of Timor-Leste, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

Timor-Leste Customs' e-Passenger Declaration asks you to declare more than 200 cigarettes or 200 grams of other tobacco, more than 2.5 litres of alcoholic drinks, goods bought abroad worth more than US$300, goods or samples for commercial use, prohibited or dangerous goods (including narcotics, ammunition, weapons and knives), and any food, plants or plant products, live animals or animal products, seafood, animal feed, biological specimens, fertiliser, soil, vaccines or medicines, including traditional medicine.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash based, that credit cards are not widely accepted, and that the ATMs in Dili can charge high fees and are often out of order. The UK Foreign Office says ATMs, banks and card facilities are not common outside municipal capitals, and advises bringing a few small (5 US dollar) notes because larger notes can be difficult to spend.

safety.text: Australia advises a high degree of caution in Timor-Leste because of crime and limited healthcare. Street-gang fighting and political demonstrations occur and minor disputes can turn violent, so avoid protests and large gatherings. Many taxis are unsafe, roads flood in the wet season, and crocodile attacks are reported in the east and along the south coast, with sightings on beaches in Dili.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says the 30-US-dollar visa on arrival is payable only in cash, and the Migration Service says card facilities are not available and ATMs and currency exchange may not be, so travellers should have the correct amount in US dollar cash.

For the overland crossing from Indonesian West Timor (Atambua–Batugade), the Migration Service says the visa on arrival is issued at land posts too, but Australia's advice still says to get a visa first.

The UK Foreign Office says roads are generally in poor condition, main routes are often single-track mountain roads that can become impassable in the rainy season, and outside Dili you should travel in convoy where possible. If you hire a car, you will likely have to hire a driver as well.

The UK Foreign Office lists dengue, chikungunya, typhoid, hepatitis and rabies (in Oecusse, Bobonaro and Covalima, and possibly elsewhere) among the health risks, and says medical services are limited, particularly outside Dili; a medical emergency is likely to mean evacuation to Australia or Singapore.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Timor-Leste?
faq.answer: Travellers who are not visa-exempt do not need anything in advance: a US$30 tourist visa on arrival, for a 30-day stay, is issued at official border posts. Citizens of the EU and the other Schengen states are visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU–Timor-Leste agreement (Ireland and the UK are not covered), and citizens of Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand are visa-free for 30 days.

faq.question: What do I need for the visa on arrival?
faq.answer: A passport valid for at least 6 months on the date of entry, US$30 in cash, and the completed online arrival declaration. Officers may also ask for evidence of funds, accommodation and evidence of departure arrangements such as an onward ticket or booking.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Timor-Leste?
faq.answer: Yes, once. Apply in person at the Migration Service Headquarters in Dili. In normal circumstances a tourist visa may be extended once only, for a further stay period of 30 days, for a US$40 fee; processing takes up to 15 days. The UK Foreign Office advises applying at least 15 days before the visa expires if possible.

faq.question: What currency does Timor-Leste use?
faq.answer: The US dollar, according to the Government of Canada, which also says the economy is primarily cash based and credit cards are not widely accepted. Older notes can be refused: Canada says many places will not accept bills issued before 2007, and the UK Foreign Office says notes printed before 2009 are usually rejected but can be changed at the Central Bank in Dili.

faq.question: Can I cross overland from Indonesia to Timor-Leste?
faq.answer: The Migration Service says the tourist visa on arrival is available at all official border posts open to foreign nationals and staffed by the Migration Service, including land crossings, and the UK Foreign Office says you can buy one at Batugade. Australia's advice still says land arrivals need a visa before arrival.
